handoff: 1 blocking (F1, AC1): story start's no-target picker offers manual units ready at non-agent steps, which the command then refuses. 4 minor/nit. Suite and typecheck green.

findings.title: story start picker offers ready non-agent units that the command refuses
findings.detail:
The `startable.applies` rule accepts `u.status === "ready" && u.effective_mode === "manual"` whatever the step type. The command (line 45) also requires `step?.type === "agent"`. Note that the view computes effective_mode with `step?.type === "agent" && attended`, so a manual story is `manual` at any step. As a result, a manual story that is ready at a check or git step is listed by `norn story start` with no target, and picking it ends in `nothing_to_open`. AC1: 'Without a target it offers only units a person can start.'
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Make the picker rule match the command's condition. For example, also require an agent step: the UnitView `start` field is set only for agent steps, or the view can expose the step type. Add a story-start test in which a manual unit ready at a non-agent step is not offered.

findings.title: An explicit slice key with --auto/--manual now edits the story; it used to be refused with story_only
findings.detail:
`resolveTarget(ctx, parseUnitKey(raw).story)` maps `norn story edit gh-8/01 --auto` to gh-8, and human.test.ts:465 pins this. B55 says only 'in a slice worktree … edit --auto|--manual act on the slice's story'. It fits B55's intent for story-only verbs, but it removes the old `story_only` guard without a spec line.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Confirm the change is intended and note it in the spec (slice 15 PRD wording), or keep refusing explicit slice keys.

findings.title: AC2's 'next tick runs gh-N in auto' is checked only through state.json mode
findings.detail:
The test asserts the mode change after a tick. It does not assert that the tick launches the agent step in auto, or holds it in manual. This gap was carried over from the old mode test.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Assert the runner launch (or its absence) on the fake runner after the tick.

findings.title: Printed commands still name the removed `norn open` and `norn workflow`
findings.detail:
`cmd.open` and `cmd.workflow` are still printed in several places: core/src/inbox/items.ts:198, core/src/decide/steps.ts:32, cli/src/commands/update.ts:47 (do_instead) and cli/src/runtime/agent-unit.ts:35,47. They now point people at unknown commands. cockpit.ts:95 detects the start item by `cmd.open()` but runs `story start`. The slice puts printed hints out of scope (slice 14), so this is not blocking here, but the two must change together.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Leave as is for slice 14; make sure that slice covers update.ts do_instead and the cockpit startsWith check.

findings.title: Two `resolveTarget`s in one file, one aliased to `pickTarget`
findings.detail:
story-edit.ts:22-23 and story-start.ts:13-14 import target.ts `resolveTarget as pickTarget` next to human.ts `resolveTarget` (Mysterious Name). The `unit_done` refusal is also duplicated with different hints: `cmd.status(t.key)` at story-edit.ts:51 and `cmd.status(t.story)` at :112.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Rename one of the two functions at its source; align the two unit_done hints.
